subject: Forgeware SDK + Redwood tracing: integration and pilot plan
messages:
From: Emily Li <emily@forgeware.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel@forgeware.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro: Forgeware SDK + Redwood tracing idea

Hi Marissa —

Great to meet on the call last week. As discussed, Forgeware's SDK clients are being used by several ISVs that also run LLM inference on Redwood. We think a tighter tracing integration between our SDK and Redwood's runtime (prefetch traces + call-level spans) would help joint customers debug prompt regressions and attribution.

High-level ask: a small pilot where we wire the Forgeware SDK to emit standardized trace spans that Redwood can ingest and correlate with request IDs. Goals:
- surface prompt/LLM call timing and token counts in the Redwood Console
- provide one-click link from Redwood trace to Forgeware request context
- keep telemetry opt-in and minimal performance overhead

Attached is a 1-pager and a draft SOW for a pilot (2 weeks of engineering + 1 week of validation). Can you confirm who at Redwood should own the runtime schema and whether we can get a sample request ID mapping?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m sync.

— Emily Li
Head of Partnerships, Forgeware Labs
attachment: Forgeware_Integration_SOW_v1.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Li <emily@forgeware.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: Forgeware SDK + Redwood tracing idea

Emily —

Really interesting proposal, thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High level: we like the value prop (better diagnostics and attribution across the stack). We want to make sure the tracing surface is:

- low-cost for hosted customers (no extra per-token charges for traces),
- compatible with our existing request ID and KV cache mapping, and
- opt-in at either customer or route level.

Jonas (cc'd) will own the runtime schema changes. Ben, can you help estimate commercial implications (is this a free pilot vs. billable integration)?

Short term next step: can we run a technical spike to define the span schema and one sample mapping? If so, propose we:
1) Kick off a 2-week eng spike (Redwood + Forgeware) to produce a trace mapping and perf numbers.
2) If perf delta < 5% and storage cost acceptable, run a 4-customer pilot for 6 weeks.

We can do a partner sync Thurs 11/19 at 10am PT — does that work?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Li <emily@forgeware.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: Forgeware SDK + Redwood tracing idea

Thanks Emily / Marissa — a few technical clarifications from the runtime side:

1) Request ID model: Redwood assigns a global request_id at the edge. Best integration is for the SDK to accept a request_id header (x-redwood-request-id) and mirror that across spans.

2) Span granularity: we recommend call-level spans per LLM invocation, plus an optional per-token emission for customers that want deep profiling. Token-level should be disabled by default.

3) KV cache correlation: if Forgeware can surface cache hits/misses as attributes on the span (cache_hit: true/false, cache_key: <hashed>) we can join that to runtime cache logs.

4) Sampling: please include a simple sampling flag (trace_sample_rate) so we can throttle.

Priyom — can you draft a minimal runtime schema we can use in the spike? I'll implement a lightweight ingest path.

-Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Li <emily@forgeware.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: Forgeware SDK + Redwood tracing idea / SOW draft

Emily — attaching a short SOW sketch and an architecture diagram (see trace-integration-arch.png) that outlines responsibilities:

- Forgeware: add request_id forwarding, implement span emitter (OTLP compatible), expose sampling flag.
- Redwood: add span ingestion endpoint behind feature flag, storage and Console linking, perf benchmarking.

Deliverables (2-week spike):
- schema.md (span fields and types),
- perf report (latency & CPU),
- PoC ingest and a Console link prototype.

Commercial ask: propose Redwood covers engineering hours for the spike, Forgeware covers customer pilot coordination. If the pilot expands, we can discuss a cost-share for storage and SLO changes.

Would you like this SOW as a Confluence page or a short DocuSign-friendly Word doc?

— Priyom Das
Principal Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this looks good. Quick notes from the Forgeware engineering team:
- OTLP emitter is already in our SDK, we need to add the x-redwood-request-id header passthrough (easy).
- We will keep token-level emission off by default.
- For the pilot customers we propose bringing one ISV that uses both our SDK and Redwood (AcmeOps) and one internal test harness.

We prefer the SOW as a Word doc for signature. Can you share a draft we can review? Also confirm Thursday 11/19 10am PT for the kickoff?

Best,
Miguel
